identity.title: Balmer Break Galaxy Candidates at z ∼ 6: A Potential View on the Star Formation Activity at z ≳ 14

paper_type_evidence.quote: Based on rich imaging data, including data obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), three candidates are identified by their extremely red $K - [3.6]$ colors

question.value: Are there Balmer break galaxies at z~6 in COSMOS, and what do they imply for the stellar mass density and the star-formation rate density of their progenitors at z>14?

evidence.quote: We search for galaxies with a strong Balmer break (Balmer Break Galaxies; BBGs) at $z \sim 6$ over a 0.41 deg$^2$ effective area in the COSMOS field.
The ALMA Band 7 observations (ID 2017.1.01259.S, P.I.: K. Mawatari) were performed in Cycle 5.
The ALMA Band 7 observations (ID 2017.1.01259.S, P.I.: K. Mawatari) were performed in Cycle 5.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs, 7.5 GHz total, centered at 336.5, 338.4, 348.5, 350.5 GHz; 15.6 MHz resolution (TDM)

evidence.quote: Four spectral windows (SPWs) with a total band width of $7.5$ GHz were set at the central frequency of $336.5$, $338.4$, $348.5$, and $350.5$ GHz.
under the antenna configurations of C43-2, C43-3, C43-4, and C43-5
The resulting synthesized beam size in FWHM was $0\ensuremath{''}.48 \times 0\ensuremath{''}.42$ with a position angle PA $\approx -78\ensuremath{^\circ}$.
We achieved $1\,\sigma$ RMS level of $\sim 30\,\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ for all the target objects.
The total on-source integration time was $38.8$ minutes for each target.
The observations were performed in April, May, August, September, and October 2018

evidence.quote: The ALMA Band 7 observations (ID 2017.1.01259.S, P.I.: K. Mawatari) were performed in Cycle 5.

evidence.quote: These color criteria are a slightly modified version of those in a previous study (cite: Mawatari+16b) to select BBGs with $T_{\rm age} \ensuremath{\gtrsim} 0.3\,{\rm Gyr}$.

method.value: SExtractor on [3.6] image, K-[3.6] > 1.75 and K-[3.6] > 2.4([3.6]-[4.5])+1.05, then remove detections in X-ray, FIR, radio and optical

key_parameters.value: Effective area 0.41 deg2; 23 color-selected, 6 remaining after multi-band selection

evidence.quote: We identified 23 objects satisfying the BBG color criteria, which are referred to as the color-selected sample in the following sections.
We estimated the completeness of our source extraction by detecting artificial sources randomly embedded in the [3.6]-band image.

analysis_steps.goal: ALMA Band 7 continuum photometry to reject dusty contaminants

method.value: CASA pipeline calibration, clean continuum, imfit with 2D Gaussians in 2 arcsec apertures at [3.6] positions; upper limits for point sources

evidence.quote: Photometry for the 12 targets was performed on the dust continuum images using CASA task `imfit` that fits the observed data within $2\ensuremath{''}$ diameter apertures
Three among the six BBG candidates (eight out of the 12 targets in total) were detected in the continuum images.

analysis_steps.goal: SED fitting with galaxy, AGN and XzLBG templates

method.value: chi2 minimization with upper-limit term, analytic scaling, 1000 MC runs (300 for AGN/XzLBG)

evidence.quote: As a result of 1,000 MC runs, we found that the BBG models at $5 \lesssim z \lesssim 8$ are significantly favored for all of the three BBG candidates.

key_parameters.value: 15 bands from F814W to ALMA Band 7

evidence.quote: The resultant number of the bands is 15: $F814W, g, r, i, z, y, Y, J, H, K_s, [3.6], [4.5], [5.8], [8.0]$, and ALMA Band 7.

assumptions.value: Chabrier IMF, Calzetti law, zero escape fraction, forbidden region A_V > max(4 SFR^0.3, 3.5), tau_SFH >= 30 Myr

evidence.quote: we define the forbidden region in the $A_V$–SFR plane as $A_V > \rm{max}(4 \times SFR^{0.3}, 3.5)$

fitting.value: Monte Carlo perturbation of fluxes; MC-best distribution gives confidence intervals

evidence.quote: The distribution of the best-fit solutions in these MC realizations defines the probability of the fitting solutions as well as the confidence intervals around the solutions.

validation.value: Tested SMC/MW laws and composite galaxy+TORUS templates

evidence.quote: We confirmed that the above results do not significantly change if we change the dust attenuation law to the SMC or MW law.

analysis_steps.goal: Stellar mass density and progenitor SFRD

method.value: n_BBG corrected for completeness; SMD from best-fit masses; SFRD = <SFR> x n_prog using 10^6 combinations of MC-best models

evidence.quote: We made $10^6$ combinations of three MC-best BBG models from the randomly selected 100 MC realizations for each object

key_parameters.value: T_BBG = T_age - T_SF - 0.2 Gyr, T_SF = 2 tau_SFH

evidence.quote: Assuming the BBG observable time duration as $T_{\rm BBG} = T_{\rm age} - T_{\rm SF} - 0.2\,{\rm Gyr}$ with $T_{\rm SF} = 2 \times \tau_{\rm SFH}$

assumptions.value: All three candidates are real BBGs at 4.8<=z<=7.8

evidence.quote: Assuming all of the three BBG candidates without ALMA detections to be passive galaxies at $4.8 \leq z \leq 7.8$

used_for.value: Pipeline calibration, clean continuum imaging, imfit photometry

evidence.quote: The data reduction and calibration were performed using the Common Astronomy Software Application (CASA) pipeline version 5.4.0.
Source extraction was performed on the SPLASH \[3.6\]-band image using SExtractor (cite: BertinArnouts96) version 2.5.0.
In photometry, we used the task “PHOT” of Image Reduction and Analysis Facility (IRAF)
The fitting code used in this study is our original SED analysis package (“PANHIT”) that is publicly available from our website
We achieved $1\,\sigma$ RMS level of $\sim 30\,\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ for all the target objects.
we estimate the number density of the BBGs as $n_{\rm BBG} = (4.9_{-2.7}^{+4.8}) \times 10^{-7}$ Mpc$^{-3}$ (comoving)
we obtained the SMD of $(2.4_{-1.3}^{+2.3}) \times 10^4\,M_\odot$ Mpc$^{-3}$
$2.4 \times 10^{-5} \lesssim {\rm SFRD} / M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc}^{-3} \lesssim 1.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at $z \ensuremath{\gtrsim} 14$

findings_qualitative.value: The three ALMA-detected candidates are dusty ULIRGs at z>~4

evidence.quote: We conclude that the three BBG candidates with ALMA detections are actually ultra luminous infrared galaxies with $L_{\rm IR} > 10^{12}\,L_{\odot}$

claims.hypothesis: Are red K-[3.6] candidates real BBGs rather than dusty galaxies?
claims.experiment: Deep ALMA Band 7 follow-up of 6 candidates plus SED fitting
claims.result: 3 undetected, favouring BBG models at 5<z<8; 3 detected as dusty
claims.finding: Three candidates are most likely BBGs, though z~0 type-2 AGN contamination cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: We therefore conclude that they are the most likely BBG candidates at $5 \lesssim z \lesssim 8$, although the contamination from dusty tori of type-2 AGNs or XzLBGs cannot be completely ruled out.

claims.hypothesis: Is BBG stellar mass density at z~6 consistent with extrapolation from lower z?
claims.finding: Consistent with the decreasing trend of passive galaxies

evidence.quote: This is consistent with an extrapolation from the lower redshift measurements.

claims.hypothesis: Does SFRD evolve smoothly beyond z=8?

evidence.quote: Our result suggests a smooth evolution of the SFRD beyond $z = 8$.

why_this_data.value: ALMA offers the depth to break the degeneracy between passive and dusty red galaxies

evidence.quote: ALMA may be the only instrument that can offer critical data to resolve the degeneracy between passive and dusty red galaxies

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: z~0 type-2 TORUS AGN and z>~17 LBG solutions judged unlikely but not excluded

evidence.quote: Such an AGN with a very low-mass BH hosted by a relatively low mass galaxy that contributes little to the whole SED (“low-mass naked” AGN) seems unlikely

limitations_admitted.value: SFRD is a lower limit; contamination by AGN not excluded; spectroscopic confirmation needed

evidence.quote: direct evidence of the BBG, i.e., spectroscopic confirmation of the Balmer break by coming *James Webb Space Telescope* ($JWST$; (cite: Gardner+06)), is needed.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only three candidates, so number density and SFRD have large Poisson uncertainty
Photometric redshifts and T_SF are template dependent
Possible marginal HSC i/z detections of BBG_22 and BBG_29
